investigacion.base:
**Gatun Lake level on Oct 31, 2026: research summary**

**What the resolution source shows (most recent version I could find)**
- I couldn't open the live index.html page directly. The ACP's linked "Gatun Water Indicators" PDF most recently showed an official Gatun water level of 84.5 ft for Sep. 22, 2026, with the last projection uploaded Sep. 22, 2026 14:30 (GMT-5). Readings in the days before that were 84.4, then 84.5 for several days, so the level was basically flat.
- On the projection chart, the y-axis runs from about 84.6 to 85.4 ft for Oct 4–Oct 29. That suggests the ACP expected a small rise into late October, roughly 84.6–85.4 ft. This is my reading of the axis range, not exact projected values.
- On that date the maximum Neopanamax draft was 48.0 ft (Panamax 39.5 ft), with a variable freshwater surcharge of 0.36%.
- The same PDF gives 5-year average levels by month (Jan–Dec): 86.5, 85.3, 84.6, 83.8, 83.7, 84.1, 84.7, 85.0, 85.2, **85.5 (Oct)**, 86.5 (Nov), 87.2 (Dec).

**Recent news (newest first)**
- **About Oct 1, 2026 (Dry Bulk Magazine):** an article said the ACP will increase daily Neopanamax transits by 10, for a total of 33 daily slots, beginning October 2026, based on present and projected Gatun Lake levels. Be careful with this one: the wording looks like a 2024 item that may have been reposted.
- **Aug 19, 2026:** the lake was about 84.35 ft as of 17 August. At that point the ACP projected a gradual decrease from about 83.85 ft to 82.94 ft for August–October 2026. The real level (84.5 ft on Sep 22) has come in above that projection.
- **Aug 6, 2026:** the ACP announced more Neopanamax draft cuts "as water levels in Gatun Lake continue to decline amid a strengthening El Niño". Draft limits went from 49.5 ft (early July) to 49.0 ft (Jul 24) to 48.5 ft (Aug 15). Later cuts brought it to 48.0 ft by September. NOAA's CPC had said there is an 81% chance the El Niño reaches "very strong" status by late 2026.
- **Earlier in 2026:** the lake hit 88.9 ft on Feb 7, which triggered spillway releases. Draft cuts began Jul 3. Reported July levels conflict: one source says 87.7 ft, but that doesn't fit the ~84 ft reported in mid-August.

**Base rates and context**
- October is normally the wettest month (around 350 mm of rain), and the lake usually rises from October into December. The 5-year average change from September to October is about +0.3 ft.
- In El Niño years the lake can stay flat or fall instead. In the 2023 drought it sat near 80 ft from June to November, and the record low is 78.3 ft (May 2016). The normal operating range is about 82–87 ft.
- The level moves slowly, typically by hundredths to a few tenths of a foot per day. Over the roughly 5 weeks from Sep 22 to Oct 31, changes are usually under ±1.5 ft unless rain is unusually heavy or unusually scarce.

**Status quo and what it implies**
- If nothing changed, the answer would be about 84.5 ft. The ACP's September projection pointed to roughly 84.6–85.4 ft by late October. The strong El Niño is the main downside risk, while normal October rains are the upside. A plausible central range is about 84.3–85.5 ft.
- **Before the deadline:** the ACP updates the level daily and the projection regularly, and may issue Advisories to Shipping on draft changes. NOAA's ENSO update is around Oct 8–9, and the next one is in mid-November, after the deadline. If the Oct 31 value isn't posted, the question uses the latest value before Nov 1.
- I found no prediction-market prices for this question.

**Suggested check:** the forecaster should pull the live ACP page for the actual early-October readings, because my latest confirmed data point is Sep 22.

**Sources:**
- [1](https://evtms-rpts.pancanal.com/eng/h2o/GatunWaterIndicators.pdf)
- [2](https://www.drybulkmagazine.com/dry-bulk/30092026/panama-canal-announces-increase-in-draft-and-daily-transit/)
- [3](https://masoceans.com/gatun-lake-water-levels-remain-well-above-the-2023-2024-crisis-period/)
- [4](https://gcaptain.com/panama-canal-to-tighten-draft-limits-again-as-water-levels-continue-to-fall/)

criterios: This question resolves as the official water level for Gatun Lake for October 31, 2026, in feet, as presented by the [Panama Canal Authority](https://evtms-rpts.pancanal.com/eng/h2o/index.html) when checked by Metaculus. If no official level is provided for that date, then the most recent value posted for a date prior to November 1, 2026 will be used. The question resolves to one decimal place.
letra_pequena: The question will not re-resolve in the event of data revisions.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 21 days, until October 31, 2026.

(b) **If nothing changed:** The last confirmed official reading in the research was 84.5 feet on September 22. Holding at that level would give 84.5 feet.

(c) **If the recent trend continued:** The modest rise from mid-August to late September would put the lake near 84.6–84.7 feet.

(d) **Experts and markets:** The research assistant’s reading of the Panama Canal Authority’s September projection suggests a late-October level around 84.6–85.4 feet, though it is not an exact projected value. No useful prediction-market price was found.

(e) **Unexpected low scenario:** Exceptionally weak October rainfall during El Niño, combined with canal water use, could bring the level below 84 feet.

(f) **Unexpected high scenario:** Sustained heavy rain could raise it above 85.5 feet. Without a confirmed October reading, I would not make either tail too narrow.

(a) **Time left:** About 3 weeks. The resolving value is for Oct 31, 2026, and the ACP posts levels daily.

(b) **If nothing changed:** About 84.5 ft. This is the last confirmed reading (Sep 22), and the level had been roughly flat around then.

(c) **If the current trend continued:** About 84.8–85.2 ft. The level held steady or edged up through September, beating the ACP's August projection of a decline toward about 83 ft. October is normally the wettest month, with a 5-year average Sep→Oct change of about +0.3 ft. The ACP's late-September projection chart spans about 84.6–85.4 ft for Oct 4–29, which implies a gradual rise.

(d) **Experts and markets:** The ACP projection implies roughly 84.6–85.4 ft by late October. A Sep 30 report says the ACP will increase draft and daily transits; the article may be a repost of a 2024 item, but if genuine it suggests the ACP is comfortable with the trend. I found no prediction markets. The question creator's range is 83.6–85.5 ft.

(e) **Low scenario:** The strong El Niño suppresses October rainfall much more than expected. The ACP keeps transits high for commercial reasons and draws the lake down, giving 83.5–84.0 ft by month-end.

(f) **High scenario:** Unusually heavy late-October rains, from a tropical wave or a strong ITCZ pass, push the lake up 1–1.5 ft. This would give 85.8–86.2 ft.

**Forecast:** I center the distribution near 85.0 ft, slightly below the 5-year October average (85.5 ft) because of the El Niño. I keep the tails wide because my latest confirmed reading is from Sep 22.

(a) The time left until the outcome to the question is known: Exactly 21 days (from October 10, 2026 to October 31, 2026).
(b) The outcome if nothing changed: 84.5 feet (the reported level as of late September 2026).
(c) The outcome if the current trend continued: The Panama Canal Authority's (ACP) baseline projection showed a modest rise into late October toward roughly 84.8 to 85.1 feet, consistent with peak rainy-season inflows somewhat outpacing transit water usage.
(d) The expectations of experts and markets: The ACP projected late October levels between 84.6 and 85.4 feet; seasonal 5-year climatology averages 85.5 feet for October; the question creator's subjective bounds anticipate values between 83.6 and 85.5 feet.
(e) An unexpected scenario that results in a low outcome: Unseasonably dry conditions driven by a rapid intensification of El Niño reduce catchment precipitation, leading transit drafts and operational outflows to deplete lake storage down toward 83.5–83.8 feet.
(f) An unexpected scenario that results in a high outcome: Several severe tropical depressions or late-season Atlantic/Caribbean storms cross Central America, bringing sustained torrential rainfall to the Gatun watershed and pushing the lake up past 85.6–86.0 feet.
